primary_claim: Training a sparse autoencoder on a quantized 1-layer transformer (gelu-2l) shows that 8-bit quantization only slightly degrades SAE reconstruction accuracy and active-feature count relative to full precision, while 4-bit quantization degrades the underlying model so severely that its activations become near-noise, causing the SAE to achieve deceptively low L1/L2 loss by zeroing out over 80% of features rather than learning genuine fine-grained features.

models.family: gelu-2l (Neel Nanda toy 1-layer transformer, full/8-bit/4-bit quantized)

effect.metric: percentage of SAE features with average activation below 1e-5, by model precision
effect.value: full precision and 8-bit show similar, gradual feature-learning trends with 8-bit only slightly behind; 4-bit shows more than 80% of features below 1e-5, indicating the SAE largely zeros out features rather than learning them

contradicts_or_qualifies: Engages with a prior critique (citing a report finding SAEs recover only 9/180 'called-shot' board features, and a commentary on Anthropic's Scaling Monosemanticity) arguing dictionary learning cannot reliably find specific features of interest, and that a feature's highest-activating examples can be unrepresentative of its typical (median) activation, as illustrated by the Golden Gate Bridge feature
stated_future_work: Train encoders for a model and each of its quantized versions and compile a large feature list to check whether specific features are missing in the 8-bit or 4-bit models
Find examples that activate a given feature in one model, then pass them through another model to see if a corresponding feature can be isolated there
Extend experiments to larger, multi-layer models using residual-stream activations and additional losses, as begun in the GitHub repo
limitations_stated: Methods like these risk finding patterns where there are none, a concern the author explicitly endorses from prior critiques
It is not clear dictionary learning/SAEs can reliably find specific 'called-shot' features of interest, including safety-relevant ones
A feature's highest-activating examples are not representative of its typical (median-activation) meaning
Comparing features across models (e.g. quantized vs. full precision) is hard because a feature found in one model's autoencoder cannot be assumed to occur at the same position in another's
quote: more than 80% of features are below 1e-5
